title: merge.Receivers follows the map-in/map-out+added-UIDs shape of its siblings
answers: How should a new mergeable AMConfigV1 resource's merge function be shaped?
Why does merge.Receivers take a map now instead of a slice?
How do I merge imported/extra config receivers into existing ones?
body: Fix pattern: `merge.Receivers` (notifier/merge/merge.go) now takes the existing resources as `map[ResourceUID]PostableApiReceiver` and a list of incoming receivers, and returns the merged map plus `[]ResourceUID` of the added/renamed keys — mirroring `TimeIntervals`, `MergeInhibitionRules`, and `MergeTemplates` instead of the old slice-in/slice-out-with-map-bridged-by-caller style. Callers that previously relied on index arithmetic over the merged slice (e.g. `merged[len(original):]`) must instead iterate the returned added-UIDs and look each up in the merged map, as done in `legacy_storage/imported.go`. Constraints: any new mergeable AMConfigV1 resource type added to MergeExtraConfig should follow this same map-in/map-out+added-UIDs signature for consistency.

Callers that previously used slice indexing (e.g., merged[len(original):]) must instead iterate the returned UIDs and look each up in the merged map, as shown in legacy_storage/imported.go. Constraint: any new mergeable AMConfigV1 resource type added to MergeExtraConfig must follow this map-in/map-out+added-UIDs signature for consistency; the old slice-in/slice-out-with-map-bridged-by-caller style is no longer the pattern. Apply when: working with pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/merge and related merge operations, or adding new mergeable AMConfigV1 resource types.
